events.boundary: Autumn 2025 to 2026: Faye learns the trading app beside her daughter.
events.description: Instead of forbidding it, Faye asks her daughter to show her how it works. They sit with it on Sunday evenings; Faye explains what she knows about order books and liquidity and, in pieces, what happened to her in 2022. Her daughter keeps a small balance and starts asking better questions. Faye starts the novel the same autumn, writing as someone walking beside a person who will go in anyway.

events.boundary: Summer 2022: two months of hiding the loss.
events.description: She keeps checking a dead balance at night, tells her partner the savings are "tied up", and stops sleeping. What changes first is her body: weight loss, a tremor in the hand that holds the phone.

events.boundary: August 2022: the confession and its aftermath.
events.description: She tells her partner at the kitchen table. He is less angry about the money than about the months of lying. Their partnership, already thin, lasts another year. What she believes changes: she no longer thinks understanding a mechanism protects her, and she stops trusting her own calm.

events.boundary: 2004-2008: the payments office as a field site.
events.description: She treats the office as fieldwork to make the loss bearable: notes on the tea round, the smokers' door, the appraisal. The notes are never written up, but the habit of seeing people as a band stays for life and becomes her way of writing.
events.region: The building society payments office, west Swindon

events.description: She learns to talk to strangers for a living, which she had never done. Visitors ask why anyone would drag a forty-ton stone across the downs; she finds herself answering that people will do almost anything to gather. She begins writing fiction in the evenings in 2024.
